Bob Onder highlights CatholicVote recognition and commemorates women's suffrage anniversary
Bob Onder, a public figure active on social media, posted several messages in mid-August 2026 reflecting on historical and contemporary issues. His posts included recognition from an advocacy group and a commemoration of a significant event in American history.
On August 17, 2026, Onder expressed gratitude for being acknowledged by CatholicVote. He stated, "It is an honor to be recognized by @CatholicVote as a leader in the fight for our children, for truth and justice, and for the American way. Truth is truth, whether it is spoken boldly or quietly, and that is a principle I will always stand by. Guided by those convictions, I".
The following day, August 18, 2026, Onder highlighted the anniversary of Tennessee's ratification of the 19th Amendment. He wrote, "On August 18, 1920, Tennessee became the 36th state to ratify the 19th Amendment, securing the three-fourths majority necessary to guarantee women the constitutional right to vote. That victory did not come easily. For decades, courageous women endured ridicule, intimidation,".
Tennessee’s decision in August 1920 was pivotal in ensuring that women across the United States gained voting rights through constitutional amendment. The process required approval from three-fourths of U.S. states before becoming law—a threshold reached with Tennessee’s ratification. The struggle leading up to this milestone involved sustained activism by women who faced significant societal resistance.
Onder’s acknowledgment from CatholicVote reflects ongoing engagement between political figures and advocacy organizations concerned with family values and civic principles.
